messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING — crashloop detected in gpu-pool-prod-eu-1. 7 pods in CrashLoopBackOff (inference-runtime). Auto-escalation to oncall.
alice-sre: ACK. I'm on it. Which nodes are showing the crashloops? link to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/crashloop
bob-runtime: seeing segfaults in vllm worker process. sample from pod inference-runtime-7f9c8: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:02:11Z] runtime: worker[3] SIGSEGV at 0x0 ip=0x7f2b6d3c4f2a sp=0x7ffd9f2a3fb0 error=invalid-read
#0  0x7f2b6d3c4f2a in fused_attention::execute(...) at fused_attention.cu:412
#1  0x7f2b6d3c5a9b in vllm::dispatch() at runtime.cc:128
```
Also seeing TensorRT log preceding crash: `ERROR: ../tensorrt/fused_kernels.cpp: invalid read when copying bindings`
```
NVRM: GPU 0000:3d:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
```
carla-ml: deploy of runtime v2.7.4 finished ~6m ago to gpu-pool-prod-eu-1. commit: 9b3f2ad. That release enabled a new fused-kernel path for attention and a TRT engine update. Rollback candidate: v2.7.3.
alice-sre: noted. dave-support, can you quantify customer impact? metrics channel?
dave-support: alerting dashboards: 503 errors spiked from 0.4% to 12.1% in the last 10m for hosted inference region eu-west. ~18 customers sent error spikes, top 3 enterprise tenants seeing >80% failed requests. snippet: 
```
requests_total: 42k
errors_5m: 5.1k (12.1%)
avg_latency_5m: 320ms -> 1.2s (tail increased)
```
alice-sre: immediate plan: isolate affected nodes, shift traffic to fallback pool, and roll runtime back if crashloops persist. Steps I will perform now: cordon node-eu-3, drain pods, scale up cpu-fallback pool, and change routing policy to prefer dedicated-cpu nodes for in-flight traffic.
alice-sre: executing: 
```
kubectl cordon node-eu-3
kubectl drain node-eu-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
kubectl -n inference scale deploy inference-runtime --replicas=0 --selector=pool=gpu-pool-prod-eu-1
kubectl -n inference scale deploy inference-runtime-cpu-fallback --replicas=10
```
bob-runtime: from core dump on one of the crashlooping pods, backtrace shows fused_attention path hitting invalid device pointer. possible race in KV cache/allocator when using TRT fused kernel. GDB snippet: 
```
#0  fused_attention::execute(...) at fused_attention.cu:412
#1  0x00007f2b6d3c5a9b vllm::dispatch()
#2  0x000055a6b1a2f7e worker_main
```
Also CUDA driver logs show: `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` in same timeframe.
infra-bot: node-eu-3 dmesg excerpt: 
```
Mar 15 14:01:56 node-eu-3 kernel: [ 1234.567890] NVRM: GPU 0000:3d:00.0: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x23:0xfffffffd)
Mar 15 14:01:56 node-eu-3 kernel: [ 1234.568901] NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 15 14:01:57 node-eu-3 kernel: [ 1235.012345] runtime[2345]: segfault at 0 ip 00007f2b6d3c4f2a sp 00007ffd9f2a3fb0 error 4
```
carla-ml: interim mitigation: disable TRT fused kernel and fall back to reference attention implementation. patch to runtime config: 
```
runtime:
  optimizations:
    tensorrt_fused_attention: false
    attention_impl: "ref"
    max_batch_tokens: 2048
```
This should avoid the invalid device pointer path while we root cause.
alice-sre: agreed. Bob, can you push a hotfix config flag to the cluster? If rollback faster, do that instead.
bob-runtime: doing rollback to v2.7.3 for inference-runtime in gpu-pool-prod-eu-1 now. command: 
```
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/inference-runtime inference-runtime=registry.redwood/inference-runtime:v2.7.3
kubectl rollout status deploy/inference-runtime -n inference
```
Rollout triggered at 14:06UTC.
dave-support: after initial rollout/cordon, error rate dropped: errors_5m -> 1.2%, affected pods now 0 crashlooping (some pods restarted stable). Notifying top customers with incident notice. Will post template update.
alice-sre: monitoring logs and metrics. Checking remaining nodes: node-eu-4 shows early signs of GPU ECC errors; cordoning it as precaution. We will keep cpu-fallback warm until full confidence.
bob-runtime: collected additional gdb output and uploaded to artifacts: https://artifacts.redwood/internal/4332109876/trace.tar.gz. Early hypothesis: new TRT path uses pooled device memory that can be freed concurrently during kv cache eviction, leading to invalid device pointer when kernel launches asynchronous ops.
carla-ml: we'll disable automatic kernel selection for the time being and add additional device pointer validity checks in next patch. Creating ticket ML-RUNTIME-341.
alice-sre: incident owner: alice-sre. action items: postmortem (alice-sre), runtime fix (bob-runtime + carla-ml), infra investigate node GPU stability (infra team), customer followups (dave-support). ETA for postmortem draft: EOD tomorrow.
alice-sre: handing off to next oncall @eve-nextoncall for overnight watch. Key things for next oncall: watch error rate on eu-west, ensure cpu-fallback remains scaled, don't uncordon nodes without infra signoff, continue rollback to any other clusters if similar symptoms appear.
eve-nextoncall: ACK. I'll monitor from 14:20-22:20UTC and will escalate if error rate >3% for 15m. I'll also coordinate with infra on the two cordoned nodes.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: Incident triage acknowledged. Pager closed for active responders; incident remains open and assigned to alice-sre. Postmortem and timeline required.
dave-support: sent customer status update to affected tenants. Template: "We experienced request failures to hosted inference in eu-west due to a runtime crash in a recent engine optimization. We've rolled back that change and traffic shifted to fallback CPUs; service is recovering. Next update in 2 hours or when we have root cause. Sorry for the disruption."
alice-sre: closing note: no data breach, no PII exfiltration detected. We'll update runbooks to include disabling TRT fused path as an emergency knob. Assigning follow-ups now.
